title: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation

definitions.Paroxysmal AF: AF that terminates spontaneously or with intervention within 7 days of onset
definitions.Permanent AF: AF accepted by patient and physician; no further rhythm-control
definitions.AF burden: Percentage of time in AF over a monitoring period
definitions.CHA2DS2-VASc: Stroke risk score: CHF(1), HTN(1), Age≥75(2), DM(1), Stroke/TIA(2), Vascular disease(1), Age 65–74(1), Sex female(1)

recommendations.text: Anticoagulation with a DOAC is recommended over warfarin in patients with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 (men) or ≥3 (women) without moderate-to-severe MS or mechanical heart valves.
Anticoagulation is not recommended for men with CHA2DS2-VASc = 0 or women with CHA2DS2-VASc = 1.
Rate control with beta-blockers or non-dihydropyridine CCBs is recommended for AF with rapid ventricular response when rhythm control is not pursued.
Catheter ablation (pulmonary vein isolation) is reasonable for symptomatic AF to improve symptoms and quality of life, and in AF-induced cardiomyopathy.
Rhythm-control strategy with antiarrhythmic drugs or catheter ablation is recommended for AF patients with HF to improve outcomes.
Amiodarone is reasonable for maintaining sinus rhythm in patients with significant structural heart disease when other AADs are contraindicated.
Flecainide or propafenone is recommended to maintain sinus rhythm in patients with AF without structural heart disease.
Left atrial appendage occlusion may be considered in patients with AF at increased risk of stroke who have contraindications to long-term anticoagulation.
DC cardioversion is recommended for patients with hemodynamically unstable AF.
Patients with AF should be evaluated and treated for risk factors and comorbidities including hypertension, obesity, sleep apnea, and alcohol use.
Digoxin may be considered for rate control when other agents are inadequate or contraindicated.
Dronedarone is recommended to maintain sinus rhythm and reduce hospitalizations in patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF without HF or LVEF <40%.

bleeding_risk.note: High bleeding risk (≥3) should prompt modifiable risk factor correction, not withhold anticoagulation
